title: Efficient and Scalable Architectures for Multi-level Superconducting Qubit Readout
problem: Superconducting transmons are multi-level systems where leakage into energy levels outside the computational subspace complicates quantum error correction (QEC). Detecting and mitigating leakage requires effective multi-level readout, but current approaches consume excessive FPGA resources and readout time.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires large-scale QEC, but hardware errors and leakage undermine reliability; efficient multi-level readout is essential for practical quantum processors.
method: Scalable three-level readout architecture using matched filters to detect relaxation and excitation error patterns, combined with a modular lightweight neural network to correct crosstalk errors. Implements bit-serial detection and integrates into off-the-shelf FPGA.
key_novelty: 60x reduction in FPGA resource usage compared to baseline through matched filter architecture and 100x reduction in neural network size via modular lightweight design for efficient multi-level readout.
contributions: Enables faster leakage detection and mitigation
limitations: Evaluation limited to superconducting qubits; applicability to other qubit modalities not discussed.
primary_theme: Efficient FPGA-based multi-level superconducting qubit readout
